title: Finite generation, dimension and finite degree of embedded curve fields
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $T$ be a nonempty integral scheme of finite type over $k$ [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Write $K(T)=\mathcal O_{T,\eta_T}$ for its function field at its generic point [def-sc-function-field], [def-sc-generic-point]. Then $K(T)/k$ is finitely generated as a field (there are finitely many elements $a_1,\ldots,a_r$ with $K(T)=k(a_1,\ldots,a_r)$), and
$$\operatorname{trdeg}_k K(T)=\dim T.$$
Here transcendence degree and dimension are [def-kun-transcendence-degree], [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Moreover, let $K/k$ and $L/k$ be finitely generated field extensions [def-pc-field-extension] of the same finite transcendence degree $d$. For every $k$-embedding $\varphi:K\hookrightarrow L$, the extension $L/\varphi(K)$ is finite [def-pc-field-tower]. No separability assumption is made.

proof.text: By [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], choose a nonempty member $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of a finite affine cover of $T$ with $A=k[a_1,\ldots,a_r]$. Such a member exists since $T$ is nonempty. By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction], $A$ is a domain and its germ map identifies $K(T)$ with $\operatorname{Frac}(A)$. Every element is $g/h$ with $g,h\in A$ and $h\ne0$. Since $g,h$ are polynomials in the $a_i$, their germs lie in $k(a_1,\ldots,a_r)$ and so does $g/h$. Conversely this subfield lies in $K(T)$. Thus $K(T)=k(a_1,\ldots,a_r)$.

source.place: Tag 0BY1, theorem-curves-rational-maps, first proof paragraph; affine calculation using the finite-type definition and Tag 01RV (morphisms-lemma-integral-scheme-rational-functions).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-closed-irreducible-dimension-trdeg] to $X=T$ and $C=|T|$, a nonempty irreducible closed subset with generic point $\eta_T$ because $T$ is integral. It gives $\dim T=\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa_T(\eta_T)$. The generic stalk $K(T)$ is a field by [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction]; its maximal ideal is zero, since any nonzero element is a unit. By [def-weil-residue-field], $\kappa_T(\eta_T)=K(T)/(0)\cong K(T)$ over $k$. Polynomial relations are preserved and reflected by this isomorphism, so the suprema of the sizes of independent subsets in [def-kun-transcendence-degree] agree. This gives the stated dimension formula.

source.place: Tag 0B1C, item-dimension-irreducible-trdeg in lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic; specialize to the whole integral scheme and identify the generic residue field.

proof.text: For the field assertion set $E=\varphi(K)\subseteq L$. Since $\varphi$ is a $k$-embedding, $K\cong E$ over $k$: for any finite tuple, a polynomial over $k$ vanishes on its image exactly when it vanishes on the original tuple, by injectivity. Thus independent subsets correspond bijectively, and [def-kun-transcendence-degree] gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_k E=d$. Apply [lem-kun-transcendence-degree-tower] to $k\subseteq E\subseteq L$: $d=d+\operatorname{trdeg}_E L$. The remaining cardinal is at most $d$, hence finite; cancellation in the nonnegative integers gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_E L=0$. The zero-degree criterion of the same node says that $L/E$ is algebraic.

source.place: Tag 030H, lemma-transcendence-degree-tower; its zero-degree consequence and invariance under the given field isomorphism.

proof.text: Choose field generators $b_1,\ldots,b_s$ with $L=k(b_1,\ldots,b_s)$. As $k\subseteq E\subseteq L$, the two inclusions $k(b_1,\ldots,b_s)\subseteq E(b_1,\ldots,b_s)\subseteq L$ show that $L=E(b_1,\ldots,b_s)$. Each $b_i$ is algebraic over $E$ by step 3. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-generators-finite-extension], applied with base field $E$ and ambient field $L$, makes $L/E$ finite. The argument used no separability.
